depression_fill.citation: Barnes, R., Lehman, C., Mulla, D. (2014). Priority-flood: an optimal depression-filling and watershed-labeling algorithm for digital elevation models. Computers and Geosciences 62, 117 to 127. doi:10.1016/j.cageo.2013.04.024.

rim_injection.name: broad_crested_weir_rim_overflow
rim_injection.equation: q_i = C_d * sqrt(g) * H_i^(3/2) per unit rim length
rim_injection.citation: Chow, V. T. (1959). Open-Channel Hydraulics. McGraw-Hill, section 3-7 broad-crested weir; Henderson, F. M. (1966). Open Channel Flow. Macmillan, chapter 6.
rim_injection.rim_elevation_rmse_z_source: USGS 3DEP QL2 1 m lidar RMSEz 0.10 m.

springs.name: Turquoise Pool
springs.injected_fraction_conservation_note: river_inflow_fraction and grid_exit_fraction are computed from the conservative absorbing-boundary MFD propagation (river cells are sinks). Their sum equals the injected fraction within the stated tolerance.
springs.river_terminal_points_note: flow_fraction_at_terminal is the per-cell MFD accumulation at the segment downstream endpoint, so these values are not additive across segments that share upstream flow. Use river_inflow_fraction for the fraction of this spring that enters the Firehole channel.

rim_overflow.note: Small pool; authored discharge shared with WP-B.

dangling_references.note: References are redirected to the nearest surviving ancestor through the removal chain, promoted from a surviving tributary at the same confluence when the main parent is gone, or dropped (orphan_segments_dropped) when the segment is a non-head reach with no surviving upstream. upstream_id is None only on head segments.

validation.per_segment_flow_note: segments[*].flow_fraction and springs[*].river_terminal_points[*].flow_fraction_at_terminal are per-cell MFD accumulations. They are not additive across overlapping D8 paths. For the fraction of each spring that enters the Firehole, read springs[*].river_inflow_fraction, computed conservatively with river cells as absorbing sinks.
